messages:
morgan: quick q — we have a tiny docs-only change in runtime docs. should we let releasebot skip the patch bump if label=docs-only?
sara: agreed it’s annoying to noise semver for docs. what's the current rule again?
james: current deploybot heuristic: if PR has only docs/chore files and no code/runtime diffs, it tags as docs-only but still creates a patch tag by default. we can change the behavior.
leo: my worry is hidden behavior causing confusion later when someone expects pinning semantics. skipping a bump means stable channel stays at previous tag, which could break reproducibility for infra that pins to latest patch.
morgan: true. maybe releasebot should still make a metadata-only release but without bumping semver? like `v1.4.2+docs.2026-03-20` or something.
sara: that could work. keep deterministic tag (so pins resolve) but indicate it's non-runtime. then package managers that interpret semver ignore buildmeta for precedence.
james: build metadata after `+` is semver-compatible and doesn't change precedence, yep. but our release tooling currently strips `+` metadata when computing channel order, so we'd need a small deploybot change.
deploy-bot: @morgan noted: current config: bump_on_merge=true, docs_skip_bump=false. Suggested change: docs_skip_bump=true, emit_buildmeta=true.
leo: operational question — if we emit `v1.4.2+docs.3141592600`, will our Dedicated capacity autoscaler treat that as same runtime as `v1.4.2`? we must ensure runtimes are compared by core semver (ignore buildmeta).
james: yes, runtime compare uses major.minor.patch. buildmeta is only for humans. I can add a test to the compare util.
sara: also need to update release notes tooling — currently it suppresses release notes for docs-only. i'd prefer we still generate lightweight release notes for audit.
morgan: rollback semantics? if someone pins to `v1.4.2+docs.x` and then we need to rollback `v1.4.2` to `v1.4.1`, will that pin follow?
joes-not-present: (lol)
leo: pins that include buildmeta should still resolve to the exact tag. But most infra pins Major.Minor.Patch; we should document that pins that include `+` are exact.
james: proposal: change releasebot rules — if PR labeled docs-only and no runtime files: 1) do not increment patch (keep x.y.z), 2) create `vX.Y.Z+docs.YYYYMMDD-HHMM` annotated tag, 3) publish skinny release notes and mark type=docs in release metadata, 4) do not trigger rollout to stable by default (opt-in flag `promote_docs=true`).
sara: +1 but make `promote_docs=false` the default to avoid surprising prod. allow `--promote` on merge when we explicitly want it.
morgan: makes sense. edge-case: security-only docs or disclosure changes — should they promote? maybe separate label `security-docs` that forces bump and promote.
leo: yes separate label for any doc that affects runtime security posture, we should bump.
deploy-bot: noted: implementing `docs_skip_bump`, `emit_buildmeta`, `promote_docs` flags. will need config PR for deploybot and a small runtime compare patch.
james: i'll own runtime compare test and deploybot config PR. sara can update release notes generator to include docs tag and type field.
sara: will do. also updating docs: "pinning and build meta" page with examples: `v1.4.2` vs `v1.4.2+docs.20260320-1430` and explain precedence.
morgan: final check — rollout window: if someone accidentally sets `promote_docs=true`, we should ensure canary window respects normal policies and not bypass canary.
leo: yes, no bypass. promote_docs just flips whether to create release into the release queue. doesn't alter rollout policy.
morgan: ok sounds good. action items: james: deploybot config + runtime compare test; sara: release notes + docs page; deploy-bot: add flags; leo: confirm Dedicated autoscales treat buildmeta as equal; i'll follow up on Monday to confirm merge. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: PR created: https://git.redwood.internal/p/deploybot/+/1842 — config change and tests.
sara: saw it, reviewing now.
james: LGTM pending one unit test tweak.
leo: looks safe to me.
morgan: thanks all. we'll retro if this causes confusion.
